title: 2005 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 6
statement: In an election, there are two candidates, \(A\) and \(B\), who each have 5 supporters. Each supporter, independent of other supporters, has a \(\frac{1}{2}\) probability of voting for his or her candidate and a \(\frac{1}{2}\) probability of being lazy and not voting. What is the probability of a tie (which includes the case in which no one votes)?

solutions.text:
63/256

The probability that exactly \(k\) supporters of \(A\) vote and exactly \(k\) supporters of \(B\) vote is \(\binom{5}{k}^{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2^{10}}\). Summing over \(k\) from 0 to 5 gives

\[\left(\frac{1}{2^{10}}\right)(1+25+100+100+25+1)=\frac{252}{1024}=\frac{63}{256} .\]
